top3.headline: Perplexity Teammates adoption doubles every ten days among $200 Max users
top3.whyItMatters: Buyers are paying premium prices for work agents; plan budgets beyond chat seats.

top3.headline: Meng To open-sources the three.js skills behind a GPT-6.2 Astra build
top3.whyItMatters: Design craft is becoming shareable agent skills that teams can reuse instead of rebuild.

top3.headline: Claude read a 1994 Jeep's engine computer and found the smog fault
top3.whyItMatters: Agents now reach physical machines through cheap parts, opening diagnostics to non-experts.

items.title: Kun Chen: with agents, build new ideas now instead of backlogging them
items.takeaway: Kun Chen says the old habit of parking new ideas in a backlog no longer fits; with agents, acting while the idea is fresh is almost always better.
items.soWhat: Planning rituals built for scarce engineering time may now slow down teams that use agents.

items.title: Alex Finn's 'reverse prompt' asks AI to find your most ambitious project
items.takeaway: The prompt asks your AI to use everything it knows about you to find the most ambitious project or question you can focus on now.
items.soWhat: AI that remembers your work can now help set priorities, not just finish tasks.

items.title: Perplexity Teammates adoption doubles every ten days among paying Max users
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says Perplexity Teammates adoption is doubling every ten days, counting only external users on the $200-a-month Max tier.
items.soWhat: Paid demand for always-on work agents is compounding; expect budget requests for agent seats.

items.title: Perplexity: all leading AI models are usable through its Orchestrator API
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says every leading AI model can be used through the Perplexity Orchestrator API.
items.soWhat: One API across models makes switching providers easier and lowers lock-in risk.

items.title: Claude read a 1994 Jeep's engine computer and found the smog fault
items.takeaway: Greg Isenberg shares how a man let Claude read his 1994 Jeep's engine computer through a $3 chip; it found the smog fault and he says the car passed. Parts cost about $15; the code is free on GitHub.
items.soWhat: Cheap hardware plus an agent turns expert diagnostics into a weekend project.

items.title: Meng To open-sources the three.js skills behind a GPT-6.2 Astra build
items.takeaway: Meng To built an endless three.js motorcycle ride with GPT-6.2 Astra using parallax and fisheye camera tricks, and open-sourced the Fisheye, Parallax and Particles & sky skills.
items.soWhat: Reusable skill files let design teams hand agents proven visual techniques instead of starting fresh.

items.title: Sam Altman credits Ven as early believer in AI on Millennium problems
items.takeaway: Sam Altman says Ven was one of the earliest believers that the then-current model could be used to solve Millennium Prize problems.
items.soWhat: OpenAI's leader is pointing at frontier math as a proof point for its models.

items.title: Hermes Agent can now run an Obsidian vault as shared memory
items.takeaway: Nous Research says Hermes Agent can now control an Obsidian vault as a shared knowledge base through the official connector, with notes kept local and private.
items.soWhat: Local knowledge bases give agents context without sending your notes to a vendor's cloud.
